impact: Two-part failure. Part 1 (harness): The cadence gate computes its target from `fps_num/fps_den = 0/1 = 0fps` (PipeWire variable-rate capture). Any non-zero observed fps fails this gate. Fix: handle fps_num=0 in validation/drivers.ts — either skip the cadence gate or use a separately configured target fps. Part 2 (workload mismatch, see ISS-003): Even if the harness target is fixed to 60fps, this run observed ~105fps from a 4K (3840×2160) capture, not 1080p60. Fixing ISS-001 alone is insufficient to unblock VAL-CAP-004 — ISS-003 must also be resolved. Blocks T-021 green verdict and T-010c gate.
resolution: Fixed in validation/drivers.ts driveValCap004 and validation/rows.ts (additive SmokeRow.nominalFps). Cadence nominal now resolves via: (1) negotiated fps if fps_num>0 && fps_den>0 (nominalSource="negotiated"); (2) row.nominalFps when negotiated is variable-rate fps_num=0 (nominalSource="row-config"); (3) when neither is available the cadence gate records "cadence (no nominal fps available)" with passed=false (nominalSource="missing") — never a silent skip or pass. thresholds.json additively records nominalFps + nominalSource. Observed mean fps and captureFormat remain written so ISS-003 (4K/~105fps workload mismatch) and ISS-002 (encoder.selected missing) remain visible. Tolerance constants (cadenceMeanToleranceFrac, cadenceP95ToleranceFrac, duplicatedPtsPerMinute) and duplicated-PTS detection unchanged. T-021 rerun 4 is still blocked by ISS-002 (encoder backend implementation under T-017a) and ISS-003 (workload mismatch decision). Verified: typecheck clean, validation:build clean, npm run build clean. No test runner is configured in the repo so no unit tests were added.
title: VAL-CAP-004 cadence gate fails against fps_num=0 (variable-rate PipeWire capture)
